stem: In the figure, angle \(ABC\) is a right angle. What is the value of \(x\)?
solution: Angles \(ABD\) and \(DBC\) together make up right angle \(ABC\), so \(27 + x = 90\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is \(360 - 27\), which uses a full turn. The two angles together make only the 90° angle \(ABC\).
explanation.B: Correct. The two angles make up the right angle: \(90 - 27 = 63\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is \(180 - 27\), which treats angle \(ABC\) as a straight angle. It is a right angle (90°).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is \(90 + 27\); the 27° angle must be subtracted from 90°, not added.

verify:
choices = {o: choices[n] for o, n in {'D': 'A', 'A': 'B', 'C': 'C', 'B': 'D'}.items()}; answer = {'A': 'D', 'B': 'A', 'C': 'C', 'D': 'B'}[answer]  # shuffled: original letters
P=figure['points']
d=lambda a,b: sqrt((P[a][0]-P[b][0])**2+(P[a][1]-P[b][1])**2)
ang=lambda a,v,b: N(acos(((P[a][0]-P[v][0])*(P[b][0]-P[v][0])+(P[a][1]-P[v][1])*(P[b][1]-P[v][1]))/(d(a,v)*d(b,v)))*180/pi)
assert abs(ang('A','B','C')-90)<0.1 and abs(ang('A','B','D')-27)<0.1
ans=90-27
assert abs(ang('D','B','C')-ans)<0.1
assert value(choices[answer])==ans
assert all(value(choices[k])!=ans for k in choices if k!=answer)
